scope: ELR-SEC-107 only: trusted guest-player and guest-team Claim issuance, inspection, consumption, legacy-token compatibility, atomic roster relinking, trusted audit writes, and the directly related Firestore client boundaries.
scopeLimit: This is not an application-wide security or Android V1 release score. Production secret provisioning, deployment, second-account Android QA, account-deletion saga work, fan voting, disputes, player profile separation, App Check rollout, and Play release gates remain outside this result.

candidate.note: Verification applies to the current local candidate layered on this base revision. No commit, push, Firebase deployment, Remote Config update, Android release, or production mutation was performed.

target.verificationSource: Repository inspection plus local Firebase Functions, Auth, Firestore, and Storage emulators using a local-only Claim secret.

summary: Guest Claim no longer trusts Flutter to issue, inspect, consume, or finalize player/team claims. Four authenticated callables derive the actor from Firebase Auth, keep the raw bearer token issuer-only, persist only its SHA-256 key/binding, validate canonical organizer and assistant authority, and transact the target, claim, roster conversion, team links, and bounded trusted audit events together. The final AppSec pass removed the global player phone/name lookup that exposed an account-existence oracle, clears guest phone data after a successful player claim, and added a fail-closed hourly quota in the existing backend-only safety quota document with actor, target, and window bounds. Legacy raw-code documents remain accepted only after strict schema, target binding, and current issuer-authority checks, then migrate atomically. Automated gates and the independent scoped AppSec review pass locally.

evidence: issueGuestClaimCode, inspectGuestClaim, claimGuestPlayer, and claimGuestTeam are authenticated callables and derive actorId exclusively from Firebase Auth
Flutter GuestClaimService and guest Claim screens use CloudSensitiveOpsService; no Claim completion fallback writes Firestore
the public audit writer remains absent from the Functions entrypoint
new tokens use HMAC-SHA-256 with a server secret of at least 32 bytes and a bounded requestId
the raw bearer token is returned only to the authorized issuer; Firestore stores the SHA-256 token document ID and target binding, never the raw token
replacement issuance expires the previous active binding and idempotent request retries return the same deterministic token without duplicate state
guest-player issuance accepts only the creator, registered-team owner or vice captain, tournament organizer, or active canonical assistant with canManageGuestRoster
guest-team issuance accepts only the guest-team creator; consumption rechecks registered-team ownership and approval state
canonical assistant authority is tournaments/{tournamentId}/assistants/{uid}; legacy assistant arrays do not grant Claim authority
player and team Claim transitions, claim consumption, membership conversion, legacy team synchronization, and audit events commit in one Firestore transaction
duplicate retries return stable alreadyClaimed or approvalRequired outcomes without duplicate roster or audit writes
legacy raw-code documents require strict schema, current target binding, and current issuer authority before atomic hash migration
audit events use a one-way token digest and exclude the raw bearer token, names, phone numbers, and conflicting account IDs
Functions unit 139/139, multi-emulator smoke, Firestore Rules Emulator 222/222, focused Flutter 30/30, and Dart analysis all pass
the local Firebase Rules audit found no remaining expression-budget warning in the final 222-test run
an independent AppSec reviewer reproduced the focused Claim tests, verified the final diff, and reported no actionable P0-P3 finding

attackMatrix.attack: unauthenticated caller invokes any guest Claim callable
authenticated unrelated player issues a Claim token
attackMatrix.expected: permission-denied without target or token mutation

attackMatrix.attack: revoked, malformed, legacy-array-only, or cross-tournament assistant issues a guest-player token
attackMatrix.expected: deny; only the active canonical assistant document is authoritative

attackMatrix.attack: caller forges playerId, teamId, target type, route target, or response target
attackMatrix.expected: derive actor from Auth and reject or return a safe conflict without identity disclosure

attackMatrix.attack: client reads, lists, creates, updates, or consumes a guest-player or guest-team Claim document directly
attackMatrix.expected: deny while the callable backend remains functional

attackMatrix.attack: client injects Claim fields, unknown fields, malformed types, oversized strings, invalid times, or forged membership identity
secondary tournament organizer changes the global captain of a shared guest team
attackMatrix.expected: deny; only the creator or canonical first-tournament authority may change global captain state

attackMatrix.expected: expire or reject without changing guest identity or roster

attackMatrix.attack: legacy raw-code document has invalid schema, target binding, or issuer authority
attackMatrix.expected: reject without migration or identity mutation

attackMatrix.attack: same token is retried or team approval is retried
attackMatrix.expected: one stable outcome with no duplicate roster, team, claim, or audit writes

attackMatrix.expected: roll back the complete Claim transaction

attackMatrix.expected: count every attempt in a backend-only hourly quota, reject above actor, target, or target-cardinality bounds, and fail closed on malformed quota state

functionsEmulatorSmoke.coverage: All ten authentication gates, trusted guest Claim issuance/inspection/player consumption/team approval and consumption, settlement roster guards, legacy safety hardening, trusted audit writes, and account deletion writes passed with exit code 0. The emulator used GUEST_CLAIM_TOKEN_SECRET=local-emulator-only-guest-claim-secret-v1; the observed Secret Manager 403 for demo-el7reef was non-fatal and no production secret was read.

firestoreRulesEmulator.warnings: No maximum-of-1000-expression or unused-variable warning remained in firestore-debug.log.

findings.finding: An independent AppSec reviewer inspected the scoped candidate and final corrective diff, reproduced the focused 33-test Claim suite, and reported no actionable P0-P3 finding.

The first independent pass found a phone-account existence oracle through distinguishable duplicatePhone responses. The global players.phone and players.nameLower lookups were removed, the guest phone is cleared on successful claim, and a regression test proves identical outcomes whether the phone exists or not.

The first independent pass found no request quota. The final candidate counts attempts in the backend-only safetyActionQuotas actor document with 240 attempts per hour, 24 per hashed target, and 128 targets per hour; invalid-token attempts count and malformed state fails closed.

remainingRisks.risk: GUEST_CLAIM_TOKEN_SECRET is not provisioned or verified in production and the four callables and Rules are not deployed. Provisioning, deployment, rollback preparation, and Android second-account QA require explicit owner authorization.

The trusted Claim quota now bounds authenticated abuse, but Firebase App Check and production abuse monitoring remain defense-in-depth work before broad public growth. They must not replace Auth, authorization, token entropy, or the server quota.
Account deletion still requires the planned resumable saga and must not be represented as atomic across Firestore, Storage, and Auth.

functions/guest_claim.js is a large security-sensitive module and is not covered by the current Dart-only hotspot budget. Split issuance, player consumption, team consumption, and legacy migration only after AppSec review, with characterization tests preserving the verified transaction contract.
Fan voting and disputes remain disabled until their trusted callable and scoped-read tickets pass.

recommendations: Keep Claim issuance, inspection, and consumption callable-only; never restore direct Flutter mutation of Claim fields or raw-code documents.
Provision GUEST_CLAIM_TOKEN_SECRET through approved production secret management only after review; never reuse the local emulator value.
Add Firebase App Check and production abuse monitoring before broad social rollout, without treating either as a replacement for authorization or the server quota.
Add Functions JavaScript to the hotspot guard and split the Claim module in a behavior-preserving maintenance change after the security checkpoint.
Deploy no Firebase or Android change from this audit without explicit owner approval, rollback preparation, and second-account Claim QA.
releaseDecision: ELR-SEC-107 is DONE locally at 5/5 within its scoped candidate. This audit authorizes no Firebase, Remote Config, Hosting, Android, Play, or iOS release; production secret provisioning, deployment, rollback preparation, and second-account Android Claim QA remain release gates.
